newsitem.title: USA: Ag-Chem cites unusual spring weather.
newsitem.headline: Ag-Chem cites unusual spring weather.

text.p: Ag-Chem Equipment Co said Monday its lower fiscal 1997 third quarter sales reflected unusual spring weather and equipment purchases made earlier in the year, followed by a strong second quarter delivery program.

"The spring of 1997 was unusual. Very favorable weather and soil conditions made spring custom application work relatively easy," said A.E. McQuinn, Ag-Chem chairman and chief executive officer. "In most of the country field work started early. The good weather permitted our customers to complete their seasons without the need to purchase more equipment," he said in a news release.

Earlier today, Ag-Chem reported sales for its third quarter ended June 30, 1997 declined to $66.4 million from $69.7 million in the same period last year. Earnings fell to $36,000 from about $1.2 million for the 1996 third quarter.
Looking ahead, Quinn said it is difficult to forecast the balance of the year. Typically, the summer can be a slow order period and customers often defer buying decisions into fall.
Ag-Chem makes and markets self-propelled, off-road chassis used for row-crop machines used to apply liquid and dry fertilizer and crop protection products.
Shares of Ag-Chem were trading off one to 22-3/4.
